inputs.cite: the audit's test points; F4 row (branch-F.md)

day.reading: the formula needs N and s and then gives an answer; the throughput question is separate
day.holds: the printed form is Kimura's Eq. 10 exactly, with both of Kimura's limits (1/2N, about 2s)

critic.reading: Hancock agrees N and s determine P(fix); it varies with demography and the DFE
critic.holds: the printed form has one N; where N_e differs from N the general form moves it (0.33 x 2s at N = 1e4, N_e = 3,300, s = 0.001), so which N is entered is a model choice (M-209)

notes: Lookup: the printed formula matches the standard new-mutation expression (initial frequency 1/(2N)) term for term. Kimura 1962 has a single N (reproducing individuals), so the printed form does not itself say whether N is census or effective; Day's text says N_e is 'estimated' and names 10,000 or 33,000 (M-114). The throughput claim that the DFE shape cancels is M-106; P(fix) against the substitution rate is M-605.
